<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9e344a9dd3ac55c5cfdc3ff29eaaa5c0ad30b00` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9d47f74605fca0a0ef7076ed529b2605b7a35107` — the merge of head `ba42fbd96c6fb14d60ccd6f5fc2b93b5bbbf23f2` into base `e9e344a9dd3ac55c5cfdc3ff29eaaa5c0ad30b00`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9d47f74605fca0a0ef7076ed529b2605b7a35107 && git checkout 9d47f74605fca0a0ef7076ed529b2605b7a35107
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e9e344a9dd3ac55c5cfdc3ff29eaaa5c0ad30b00 ba42fbd96c6fb14d60ccd6f5fc2b93b5bbbf23f2 && git checkout -B drift-repro e9e344a9dd3ac55c5cfdc3ff29eaaa5c0ad30b00 && git merge --no-ff ba42fbd96c6fb14d60ccd6f5fc2b93b5bbbf23f2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e9e344a9dd3ac55c5cfdc3ff29eaaa5c0ad30b00
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e9e344a9dd3ac55c5cfdc3ff29eaaa5c0ad30b00` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ba42fbd96c6fb14d60ccd6f5fc2b93b5bbbf23f2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-sibling-restrict.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/cascade-delete-restrict-same-parent-real-driver.integration.test.ts + .changeset/26718-restrict-over-own-cascade.md (prose face, read for ②), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (`deleteData`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts (`deleteManyData`, `runDeleteManyLoop`, `runAtomicBatch`), packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/crud-nodes.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-delete-dispatch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx, skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md

Read at 2026-10-27T19:10Z: card #26718 (body, triage `6446928568`, claim `6448161362`, os-dev-report `6451083716`, seat ruling `6451117438`), PR #26864 body and file list, `git diff origin/main...ba42fbd96c` (merge-base `0ea90c7a18`, 4 files, +587/−80), the cited code at the head via `git show`, and the head's check-runs. Nothing built, run or re-run. Rendered by the seat's subagent.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set change the diff implies (one, narrowing):** a by-id delete of record R now refuses `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` where it answered success, when a row the cascade would remove only because R goes holds an authored `restrict` (resolved behaviour of `cascadeRelationBehavior`: `lookup`/`tree` with `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'`, or `master_detail` with `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'`) pointing at R, directly or at a member in R's own cascade reach. Judged RIGHT: it is exactly the card's reproduction (child with master_detail + restrict lookup to one parent, both field orders) plus the grandchild case, and it is the triage done-when (`6446928568`: "a restrict on any path refuses"), read by ruling `6451117438` as "any path through the protected record".

**Public-surface changes:** none. `CascadeDeleteSet.cascadeEdges`, `cascadeMemberKey`, `cascadeReachOf`, `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade`, `deleteRestrictedError` are module-private / `private` members of `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`; no export, type, schema key or error code is added. The refusal envelope is the pre-existing `DELETE_RESTRICTED` (ADR-0112): the builder body lifted into `deleteRestrictedError` is byte-identical to main's inline block modulo `throw err` → `return err` (78 lines compared whitespace-stripped). RIGHT.

**Mechanism, read in the cited code.** `cascadeDeleteRelations` (engine.ts 18731) → `collectCascadeDeleteSet` (18799, read-only, now records every cascading edge, including one to a row already in the set) → NEW `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade` (19431, read-only) → `cascadeDeleteSets.run(walkReferencingRelations)` (first write). The new step iterates root + every edge target, and for each member whose object has a `restrict` relation from an object that has a member in the set, probes that relation and refuses only rows inside `cascadeReachOf(member)`. A nested delete the walk issues joins the inherited set (18761) and skips the step, which is correct: the root already judged every member's reach. The walk's phase-2 `restrict`/`set_null` filter against rows outside the set is unchanged (19288-19291).

**Seat question 1 (letter A, #22305 pin).** Confirmed. `engine-cascade-delete-sibling-restrict.test.ts`: the 487 lines on main are byte-identical in the head (`diff` of main's file against the head's first 487 lines: empty); the diff is a pure append of 105 lines (one new `describe('[#26718] …')` with 5 cases: card shape × 2 field orders, grandchild restricting the root, grandchild restricting the member above it, 2 controls). **No existing assertion was loosened, removed or flipped.** The two #22305 pins the fix could have disturbed stay green by construction: (a) "an AUTHORED restrict between two members does not refuse" (quote → contact, both details of the account): the quote is not in the contact's `cascadeReachOf` (no cascading edge contact → quote) and no restrict relation points at the account from the quote, so neither member refuses; (b) "a member holding a required lookup to the ROOT does not refuse the root" (ledger): `cascadeRelationBehavior` returns `set_null` for a required lookup (the escalation happens later, in the walk), so the new step never probes it. The new refusal is limited to rows whose membership in the set passes through the protected record (its `cascadeReachOf`), or rows outside the set (phase 2, unchanged). One consequence worth naming, consistent with A: a row reached by TWO paths (through the protected record and through another member) is in the protected record's reach and refuses; the dev's comment at 18845 states this on purpose. Report line: 27/27 on this head; ablation of the one call reds exactly the 4 new non-control cases and no #22305 pin.

**Seat question 2 (every delete door).** Every door that deletes by id reaches `ObjectQL.delete` with a scalar `where.id` (`resolveEngineDeleteDispatch` → `by-id`), which calls `cascadeDeleteRelations` inside `runByIdDelete` (engine.ts 20285) and therefore now refuses the card's shape:
- `ObjectQL.delete(object, { where: { id } })` — the walk itself (unit pins).
- `protocol.deleteData` (protocol.ts 13883-13888) → `engine.delete(where:{id})` — refuses (real-driver pin, `developerMessage` contains `via f_lookup`).
- `protocol.deleteManyData` → `runDeleteManyLoop` (protocol-batch-data.ts 863) → `engine.delete(where:{id})` per id — refuses per id (real-driver pin: `success:false, succeeded:0, failed:1`, both rows still present).
- REST `DELETE /api/v1/data/:object/:id`: `packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts` 532 → `p.deleteData`; the runtime `/data` domain `packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts` 354 → `actionExec.callData('delete')` → `protocol.deleteData` (action-execution.ts 629), or the no-protocol fallback `ql.delete(where:{id})` (676) — both by id, both refuse.
- REST `POST /api/v1/data/:object/deleteMany`: `packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts` 635 → `p.deleteManyData` — refuses per id.
- Import undo (`data-action-routes.ts` 714) → `p.deleteData` per created id — refuses.
- Action facade `delete(object, idOrIds)` (action-execution.ts 2140) → `ql.delete(where:{id})` per id — refuses.
- Flow `delete_record` with `multi` off (crud-nodes.ts 882): the filter must name one id or the engine refuses the predicate shape, so it is by id — refuses.
- CLI `data delete` → `client.data.delete` → the REST door above.

**Predicate delete.** `engine.delete` with `multi: true` and a non-id `where` routes to `driver.deleteMany` and never calls `cascadeDeleteRelations` (engine.ts 20325-20327; dispatch table in `engine-delete-dispatch.ts` 274-290). Pre-existing on main, unchanged by this diff, documented in the `cascadeDeleteRelations` docblock and pinned by `engine-cascade-delete-atomic.test.ts` 407-421 ("opens no transaction when … the delete is by predicate"). It is NOT reachable through the HTTP data doors: `deleteManyData` fails closed on anything but a list of scalar ids (protocol-batch-data.ts 806-815) and `deleteData` takes one id. Precision on the dev's "not reachable through a public door": it IS reachable by an authored flow `delete_record` node with `multi: true` and a non-id filter (crud-nodes.ts 845-882, the author's declared bulk intent), and by in-process system callers (`lifecycle-service.ts` 1691, `plugin-auth/organization-delete.ts` 279-288, `suspended-run-store.ts` 516). All pre-existing, outside the card's measured reach (`DELETE /api/v1/data/…`), and not a defect this PR introduces or widens. Escalated in ③ as a note for the seat, not a blocker.

**Seat question 3 (atomicity).** Yes. The step is read-only and runs before `walkReferencingRelations` and before the parent's own `driver.delete`, inside `runByIdDelete`; under `planCascadeAtomicity === 'atomic'` that is inside `this.transaction(...)`, and under `'none'`/`'split'` nothing has been written when it throws either way. Pins: unit cases assert `driver.writes` is `[]` and every row count intact; real-driver cases read counts out of the driver (parent 1, mid 1, leaf 1 for the grandchild case; parent 1, child 1 for the card shape and the bulk door). For `deleteManyData`: each id is its own by-id delete, so each refusal leaves that id's parent, child and grandchild in place; an earlier id in a non-atomic list that already succeeded stays deleted and is reported per row (`succeeded`/`failed`, the #4435/#19412 contract), and with `options.atomic: true` the whole batch rolls back through `runAtomicBatch` (protocol-batch-data.ts 198, #4620). Both batch semantics are pre-existing and unchanged.

**Seat question 4 (controls).** Yes, exactly as on main. `set_null`: the new step probes only relations whose resolved behaviour is `restrict`, so a `set_null` relation (optional lookup, or a required lookup before escalation) is never touched; the walk's set_null branch is untouched by the diff; #22305 pins "issues no set_null write against a member" (both registration orders) and "still clears an outside optional lookup" stand unchanged. Plain `master_detail` cascade with no restrict: no restrict relation exists, `restrictingInto` returns `[]`, the step is a no-op; pinned on the real driver ("a plain master_detail with no restrict still cascades", counts 0/0). Two-different-parents control: the child is outside the guarded parent's cascade set, so phase 2 refuses it as before; pinned on the real driver and in the unit file ("deleting the restricted record of a pledge owned elsewhere still refuses"). Ablation evidence in the report: the controls stay green with the step no-op'd, so they are not carried by the new code.

**Seat question 5 (dogfood battery).** Met. The report's `dogfood_battery` line names `ba42fbd96c6fb14d60ccd6f5fc2b93b5bbbf23f2`, `os-verify-lock VERDICT command-exit 0`, `Test Files 314 passed | 3 skipped (317)`, `Tests 2609 passed | 20 skipped (2629)`, no shard named; the voided first run (cli build exit 2 under a forwarded flag) is disclosed and was rerun on the same head.

**Check-runs on the head (gate verdicts), read at 2026-10-27T19:10Z:** 42 runs; 22 `success` (incl. Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI/release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped ×3, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs affected, Auto Label, filter, Test UI); 11 `skipped` by path filter or opt-in (UI jobs, Build Docs, Dogfood shards/Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness); 10 still `in_progress`: Test Core (1/8)…(8/8), Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. No failure read. The verdict below stands on what is read; a red among the 10 in-progress runs reopens it.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/26718-restrict-over-own-cascade.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`. Correct per AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3: a non-protocol change, breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The body carries both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no (narrowing) — …`, `Metadata-protocol: none`), the `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing` banner, the Before/Now/Unchanged/Who-sees-it paragraphs, the remedy, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which is right: no authorable key, export or type is added, removed or re-shaped, so there is nothing for a migration to rewrite and no tombstone is owed. The PR body carries the same two lines (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) and the title is `fix(objectql)!:`. `@objectstack/runtime` gains a test file only and publishes nothing, so one changeset is correct. `Check Changeset` on the head: success. `Skills-docs: none` holds: `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx` 312/334 and `skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` 173-185 already teach that `restrict` refuses the parent delete while a referencing row exists; nothing taught changes.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches what the diff publishes: one by-id delete that succeeded now refuses 409; nothing widened.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (sibling-held authored restrict: A keep vs B absolute): **answered** by seat ruling `6451117438`, letter A. The diff is A as shipped: the reach filter in `refuseRestrictsInsideOwnCascade` (`if (!reach.has(childName)) continue;` and `cascadeSetHas(reach, …)`) keeps the #22305 authored-member pin, which is unchanged in the file. No pin change is owed; the B follow-up is a separate triage card if a real app reports it.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (predicate delete runs no walk): **answered** — pre-existing on main, documented and pinned, unchanged here, not reachable through the HTTP data doors. **Escalated as a note:** the dev's "not reachable through a public door" is true of the data doors but not of an authored flow `delete_record` with `multi: true` (and in-process system callers); whether that pre-existing contract wants a card of its own is the seat's call, outside this PR.
- Dev flag "no save-time refusal added": consistent with the claim's ruling (`6448161362`: no save-time refusal, that would be a spec card) and with the lane red line (no `packages/spec/**`, no `ui/**` in the file list).
- Dev flag "overlapping open PR #26792 touches `engine.ts` in a different region": not an input of this review; the diff's hunks are at 4518-4551, 18710-18775, 18803-18855, 19253-19305, 19396-19592, which the PR body states is away from #26792's validate-body cut. Not re-measured here.
- Dev flag "`check:watch-hint-literal` rerun / `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needs the unshallowed clone": local-gate notes; the head's CI check-runs are the gate verdicts and none of the completed ones is red.
- Deviation from the claim's expected file surface: none (`packages/objectql/src/**`, its tests, a `patch` changeset, plus one runtime integration test, which the claim's "its tests" covers).
